document.title: SRS: ACME Municipal Library Information System
document.text:
# 1 Introduction
## 1.1 Purpose
This SRS specifies the requirements for developing the ACME Municipal Library Information System (ACMELIS). It is intended for the ACME software engineers who will design and implement ACMELIS, and for the team that will develop the acquisition and withdrawal module.
## 1.2 Scope
ACMELIS is a web-based information system for municipal library members (any resident of the municipality) and library staff. ACMELIS will handle book reservations, loans, and returns; related user notifications; and the suspension of users who return books late. ACMELIS will not handle the entry, modification, and deletion of library users and books, nor their acquisition and withdrawal. ACMELIS will not support physical operations, such as delivering books to users.
## 1.3 Product Overview
### 1.3.1 Product perspective
The system has the following interfaces.
- SMTP software, see [REF-01]. - SMS sending service, see [REF-02]. - Letter printing service, see [REF-03].
### 1.3.3 User characteristics
Users include municipal library members of any age, education level, and computer familiarity, as well as library staff. Many users do not have an e-mail address, and others, such as elderly people, prefer to receive letters, so notification types (e-mail, SMS, or letter) differ among users.
### 1.3.4 Limitations
ACMELIS provides a web interface only for all operations: Reservation, loan, return, and cancellation of suspensions.
## 1.5 SRS Overview
This SRS follows the outline of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018. The sections of the outline that do not appear have been omitted for simplicity; notice that this reason is valid only in the framework of this academic course. Requirements are identified as FUN(xx) for functional, PER(xx) for performance, and QUA(xx) for quality requirements. Each requirement is a singular sentence that uses the verb "shall".
# 2 References
[REF-01] RFC 5321, Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, IETF, 2008.
[REF-02] ACME Municipality SMS Gateway Interface Guide, version 1.0, ACME Municipality IT Services, 2024.
[REF-03] ACME Municipality Letter Printing Service Interface Guide, version 1.0, ACME Municipality Mail Service, 2024.
# 3 Specific requirements
## 3.1 Functions
FUN(01) The system shall allow a user to reserve a book, whether or not the book is on loan.
FUN(02) The system should allow a user to consult their reservations.
FUN(03) The system shall allow a user to cancel or extend a reservation.
FUN(04) The system shall allow each user to choose the notification type (e-mail, SMS, or letter).
FUN(05) The system shall notify the user with the oldest reservation, before the loan due date, using the chosen notification type.
FUN(06) The system shall allow library staff to request the purchase of a book that has more than 5 reservations per week during four consecutive weeks.
FUN(07) The system shall allow the librarian to register a loan requested by a user at the library.
FUN(08) The system shall set the loan period to 21 days for every user.
FUN(09) The system shall not allow a suspended user to use the system.
FUN(10) The system shall send the overdue notices to the user, with the notification type chosen, using the template defined in [REF-04].
FUN(11) The system shall run on an Apache Tomcat 9 web server with a PostgreSQL 14 database.
## 3.2 Performance requirements
PER(01) The system shall serve 20 simultaneous users with a response time of less than 10 seconds.
## 3.7 Software system attributes
QUA(01) The authentication mechanism shall resist brute-force attacks.
QUA(02) The system shall guarantee that every SMS notification is received by the user.
# 5 Appendixes
## 5.1 Assumptions and dependencies
The IT department of the ACME Municipality is responsible for the initial data load. ACMELIS depends on the library's loan module, which the ACME Municipality supplies.
## 5.2 Acronyms and abbreviations
**SMTP:** Simple Mail Transfer Protocol.
**SRS:** Software Requirements Specification.
